summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening right-sided headache and eye pain, found to have a new nasopharyngeal mass on MRI, raising concern for recurrent lymphoma given her history of DLBCL. She also had severe sinusitis with purulent drainage. A biopsy was performed, revealing CD30-positive cells of uncertain origin, with cultures growing Streptococcus pneumoniae and MRSA. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin after discontinuing Levaquin due to resistance. Her symptoms improved, and repeat imaging showed slight improvement in sinus disease but a stable nasopharyngeal mass. Bone marrow biopsy was performed but results were pending at discharge. She completed a week of inpatient antibiotics and was discharged on a 14-day course of oral vancomycin with follow-up arranged in oncology, ENT, and infectious disease. Chronic conditions including CVID, diabetes, and chronic pain were managed throughout.
